UGC Rates 2026: How Much to Charge (US, Canada and Europe)

Quick Answer

Beginner UGC creators in the US, Canada and Europe usually charge $50 to $150 per video for organic use, then add fees for paid ad usage, raw footage and extra hooks. Across 81 paid US UGC gigs listed on Newcollab in September and October 2026, the median posted pay was $150, with the middle half of offers between $35 and $600.

UGC pricing confuses most new creators because it is not based on followers. A brand buying UGC is paying for footage it will run on its own ads and pages, so your rate depends on the work, the usage and your results, not your audience size. This guide covers what brands actually pay, a starter rate card, how to price usage rights and add-ons, how to negotiate, and what Canadian creators should know.

Table of Contents

1. What brands pay for UGC right now
2. A starter UGC rate card
3. Usage rights and add-ons
4. Gifted vs paid: when to say yes
5. How to negotiate UGC rates
6. Retainers and long-term deals
7. Notes for Canadian creators
8. Notes for UK and EU creators
9. What to put in writing
10. FAQ

1. What Brands Pay for UGC Right Now

We looked at the 81 paid UGC gigs for US creators that Newcollab listed in September and October 2026. These are real postings from brands and agencies hiring UGC creators, collected from job boards and brand programs.

What we measuredResult
Median posted pay$150
Middle half of offers$35 to $600
Most common pay structuresFlat fee per video; monthly retainer for a set number of videos; base fee plus a bonus per 1,000 views
Who was hiring mostConsumer apps (fitness, finance, alarm and social apps) and DTC product brands

Two things stand out. First, the range is wide because the offers are not like for like: a $450 posting can be a month of daily videos, while a $40 posting can be one clip. Always work out the pay per finished video before you compare. Second, performance pay is spreading: app brands in particular offer a base fee plus a bonus tied to views. That can pay well if you are good at hooks, but make sure the base alone covers your time.

2. A Starter UGC Rate Card

Followers do not set UGC prices, but brands still look at them when you post the video on your own account too. These are the starting floors the free Newcollab UGC portfolio builder suggests. They are conservative on purpose: raise them once brands accept them without negotiating.

Your followersReelTikTokPhoto
Under 2,000$50$45$25
2,000 to 5,000$80$75$40
5,000 to 10,000$120$110$55
10,000 to 20,000$180$160$80
20,000 to 50,000$280$250$120
50,000+$450$400$180

For UGC the brand only posts on its own channels (you do not post it), price on the work instead: start around $75 to $150 per edited video with one hook, then add the extras below. Raise your base after every 3 to 5 completed briefs, or as soon as you are booked out.

Put Your Rates Where Brands Can See Them

Brands hire faster when rates are on the page. The free builder suggests a floor for your follower count and publishes a rate card with your samples.

3. Usage Rights and Add-Ons

The base rate pays for making the video. These extras pay for what the brand does with it. They are where experienced UGC creators earn most of their fee.

Add-onWhat it meansCommon starting point
Paid usage (30 days)The brand runs your video as a paid ad+30 to 50% of base
Paid usage (90 days / 6 months)Longer ad runs+60 to 100% of base
Perpetual usageThe brand can use it forever2 to 3 times base, or decline
Whitelisting / Spark AdsAds run from your account handleMonthly fee, often +50% of base per month
Extra hookSame video, new first 3 seconds+$15 to $40 per hook
Raw footageUnedited clips they can re-cut+25 to 50% of base
Rush (under 72 hours)Faster turnaround+25%
ExclusivityNo competitor work for a periodPrice per month of exclusivity

These are starting points, not rules. What matters is that you never give paid usage, raw footage or exclusivity for free: they are the parts of the deal that are worth most to the brand.

4. Gifted vs Paid: When to Say Yes

  • Say yes to gifted for your first 3 to 5 collabs, when the product is something you would buy anyway, and when you keep the right to use the clips in your portfolio.
  • Ask for payment once you have a portfolio, when the brief asks for more than one video, or when the brand wants to run your video as an ad.
  • Turn it down when a brand asks for paid usage, raw footage or exclusivity in exchange for a free product.

Need gifted collabs to build that first portfolio? Start with brands that accept creators with no followers, then move to brands that pay for UGC.

5. How to Negotiate UGC Rates

Before you quote anything, get answers to five scope questions:

  1. How many videos, and how long?
  2. Will the brand run it as a paid ad, and for how long?
  3. Do they need raw footage or extra hooks?
  4. How many rounds of revisions?
  5. When do they need it, and when do they pay?

Then quote a package, not a per-video number. Packages make the conversation about value and make it easy for the brand to say yes to the middle option:

PackageIncludesExample price
Starter1 video, 1 hook, organic use, 1 revision$120
Ads1 video, 3 hooks, 30 days paid usage, captioned + clean$220
Bundle3 videos, 3 hooks each, 30 days paid usage, raw footage$550

When a brand says the budget is lower, cut scope instead of price: fewer hooks, organic use only, or no raw footage. A short reply works well:

Thanks for sharing the budget. For $100 I can do one video with one hook for organic use on your channels. If you want to run it as an ad, the Ads package at $220 adds three hooks and 30 days of paid usage. Happy to start either this week.

Include your UGC portfolio link in every quote. Brands negotiate less when they have already seen the work.

6. Retainers and Long-Term Deals

The best UGC income is repeat work. Once a brand has bought two or three videos and liked the results, offer a monthly package: for example 4 videos with 2 hooks each per month, 30 days of paid usage included, at a 10 to 15 percent discount on your per-video price, billed at the start of each month.

  • Send a short monthly recap: what you made, and any results the brand shared.
  • Pitch next month's ideas before they ask.
  • Reply within a business day and deliver early when you can.
  • Review your rate every 3 to 6 months. Results you can point to are the best reason to raise it.

7. Notes for Canadian Creators

  • Quote US brands in USD and Canadian brands in CAD, and write the currency next to every number.
  • Use a payment method that does not lose much on conversion; compare fees before you accept your first US payment.
  • Track your revenue for GST/HST. Once you pass the small supplier threshold set by the Canada Revenue Agency, you need to register and charge it.
  • Many US brands ask for a tax form before paying. Ask which one they need for a Canadian creator before you invoice.

Looking for Canadian brands? See our list of Canadian brands that work with creators.

8. Notes for UK and EU Creators

UK and EU brands pay UGC creators on the same model (base fee plus usage), and many also hire from the US. A few things differ:

  • Quote UK brands in GBP, EU brands in EUR, and US brands in USD. Convert the rate card above at today's rate rather than copying the dollar figures.
  • Label anything posted on your own account as an ad. In the UK the ASA and CMA guidance expects a clear #ad up front; most EU countries have similar rules.
  • Watch the VAT threshold in your country. In the UK it is set by HMRC; in the EU each country sets its own, so check before your UGC income grows.
  • Usage rights in contracts often mention specific countries or regions. If a US brand wants to run your ads in Europe too, that is wider usage and worth more.

9. What to Put in Writing

Even a short email agreement protects you. Make sure it states:

  • Deliverables: number of videos, length, hooks, captioned and clean versions.
  • Usage: organic only or paid ads, which platforms, and for how long.
  • Revisions: how many rounds are included.
  • Payment: amount, currency, due date (net 15 is fair for small brands) and any deposit.
  • Kill fee: what you are paid if the brand cancels after you have filmed.
  • Portfolio rights: you can show the work in your portfolio.
  • Disclosure: how the content should be labeled if it is posted on your account.

Related: UGC contracts and usage rights, UGC jobs for beginners and the best UGC platforms for creators.

FAQ

How much should a beginner UGC creator charge?

Most beginners in the US, Canada and Europe start between $50 and $150 per video for organic use, then raise prices after 3 to 5 paid briefs. Newcollab's starter floor is $50 per Reel and $45 per TikTok, which you should raise as soon as brands accept it without pushback.

Do UGC creators get paid per video?

Usually, but not always. Among 81 paid US UGC gigs listed on Newcollab in September and October 2026, offers came as a flat fee per video, a monthly retainer for a set number of videos, or a base fee plus a bonus per 1,000 views.

How much should I charge for usage rights?

A common starting point is to add 30 to 50 percent of your base rate for 30 days of paid ad usage, and more for longer periods or perpetual rights. Organic posting on the brand's own channels is usually included in the base rate.

What currency should I quote UGC rates in?

Quote in the brand's currency: USD for US brands, CAD for Canadian brands, GBP for UK brands and EUR for EU brands. Check the exchange rate when you send the quote and write the currency next to every number, so a CAD or EUR figure is never read as USD.

Should I ever do UGC for free?

Gifted collabs (product plus shipping) are a fair way to build your first portfolio clips. After 3 to 5 gifted collabs, start charging. Never give paid ad usage rights for a free product.
